what.text: Dihexa is a small, chemically modified peptide: N-hexanoic-Tyr-Ile-(6) aminohexanoic amide. It was made at Washington State University from angiotensin IV, a fragment of the angiotensin hormone system that also controls blood pressure, by trimming it and changing its ends so that it lasts longer, can be taken by mouth and can reach the brain.

src.label: McCoy et al., J Pharmacol Exp Ther, 2013

what.text: Its developers designed it as a possible treatment for dementias such as Alzheimer's disease. FDA's records call it dihexa acetate.

src.label: McCoy et al., J Pharmacol Exp Ther, 2013
Wright, Kawas and Harding, Prog Neurobiol, 2015

what.text: How it acts, according to animal and lab studies:

items.text: Its developers reported that it binds hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) and increases signalling through HGF's receptor, c-Met, which helps form new connections between nerve cells. The main paper making this claim was retracted in 2025.

src.label: Benoist et al., J Pharmacol Exp Ther, 2014 (retracted)
J Pharmacol Exp Ther, retraction notice for Benoist et al. 2014

items.text: In the developers' tests, it showed "marked synaptogenic activity": it increased the formation of new connections between nerve cells.

src.label: McCoy et al., J Pharmacol Exp Ther, 2013

what.text: No study of dihexa in people has been published. The paper that set out its mechanism was retracted in 2025.

research.text: No published human studies found as of November 1, 2026. FDA has not identified any human exposure data for dihexa acetate by any route. All the evidence below is in animals, fish or cells.
A PubMed search returned 19 records and none was a study in people. ClinicalTrials.gov lists no trial.

research.title: First description of dihexa, 2013

facts.v: McCoy AT, et al. J Pharmacol Exp Ther 2013;344(1):141-54
rats given scopolamine to impair memory, and aged rats
Morris water maze (a spatial memory task), and synapse formation

research.found: The authors report that dihexa, given by mouth, reversed the memory deficits in both rat models and increased synapse formation.

src.label: McCoy et al., J Pharmacol Exp Ther, 2013

research.text: In September 2021 the journal published a notice of concern about this 2013 paper.

src.label: J Pharmacol Exp Ther, notice of concern on McCoy et al. 2013

research.title: How dihexa acts, 2014

facts.v: Benoist CC, et al. J Pharmacol Exp Ther 2014;351(2):390-402
binding tests, cell studies and rat memory tests
binding to HGF, c-Met activation, new synapses, and water-maze learning when HGF was blocked

research.found: The authors reported that dihexa acts through HGF and c-Met. The journal retracted the paper in April 2025.

src.label: Benoist et al., J Pharmacol Exp Ther, 2014 (retracted)
J Pharmacol Exp Ther, retraction notice for Benoist et al. 2014

research.text: In April 2025 the same journal also retracted two earlier papers by this group on angiotensin IV analogs and the HGF/c-Met system (2011 and 2012).

src.label: J Pharmacol Exp Ther, retraction notice for Kawas et al. 2012
J Pharmacol Exp Ther, retraction notice for a 2011 paper from the same group

research.title: Alzheimer's model mice, 2021

facts.v: Sun X, et al. Brain Sci 2021;11(11):1487
APP/PS1 mice, a genetic model of Alzheimer's disease
water-maze memory, nerve-cell counts, brain inflammation and PI3K/AKT signalling

research.found: The authors report better spatial learning, more nerve cells and less brain inflammation with dihexa.

src.label: Sun et al., Brain Sci, 2021

research.title: Hair cells in zebrafish, 2015

facts.v: Uribe PM, et al. Front Cell Neurosci 2015;9:3
larval zebrafish, whose lateral-line hair cells resemble inner-ear hair cells
survival of hair cells exposed to the antibiotics neomycin and gentamicin

research.found: Dihexa protected hair cells from these antibiotics in the fish.

src.label: Uribe et al., Front Cell Neurosci, 2015

research.text: A 2021 rat study tested dihexa, stem cells and G-CSF after cutting and repairing the sciatic nerve, measuring limb function for 16 weeks.

src.label: Ann Med Surg, 2021 (rat sciatic nerve study)

us.text: Not FDA approved for any use, and no human study has been published. Dihexa acetate was in FDA's Category 2 (substances that may pose significant safety risks) before its compounding nominations were withdrawn. It is not in the HHS peptide policy of October 2026. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: FDA lists dihexa acetate among substances that were in Category 2 whose nominations were withdrawn. FDA says it "has not identified any human exposure data" for dihexa acetate by any route, and "lacks important information regarding any safety issues raised by dihexa acetate, including whether it would cause harm if administered to humans."

after.text: Dihexa is not named on the WADA Prohibited List for 2026 or 2027. WADA class S0 bans at all times any pharmacological substance not covered by another class and with no current approval by any government health authority for human therapeutic use, including drugs still in development. For 2027, WADA adds "peptides" to the examples in S0. The lists do not say whether dihexa falls under S0.
